actor: Humanoid-platform control and robot-software engineering team (a bipedal-humanoid vendor or its onboard-platform group)
job: Porting whole-body manipulation policies off a tethered workstation onto the robot's onboard Thor-class module so they run at control-loop rates untethered.
outcome: A whole-body manipulation task running with its policy fully on the robot's onboard compute, no external workstation in the control loop.
motivation: Onboard autonomy is the field's new bar, and untethering is the headline capability that differentiates their platform to developers and buyers.

task.who: the platform's motion-control and onboard-inference engineering sub-team
task.what: port whole-body manipulation policies onto the onboard compute module
task.where: the robot's onboard Thor-class module and its control stack
task.why: untethered onboard autonomy differentiates the humanoid platform
task.how: NVIDIA Thor module plus on-device inference optimization

actor: Robot-learning research group (an embodied-AI lab or humanoid-vendor research team building manipulation skills)
job: Training and running whole-body manipulation policies directly on the robot, then documenting the untethered on-robot result in a paper, demo, or writeup.
outcome: A published demo, technical writeup, or deployment reporting whole-body manipulation executed fully on the robot's onboard compute, explicitly untethered.
motivation: Being first to report untethered on-robot whole-body manipulation is a citable milestone as the field's bar moves past tethered demos.

task.who: the lab's robot-learning and on-robot experimentation sub-team

task.where: an open humanoid developer platform carrying Thor-class compute
task.why: first untethered on-robot result is a citable milestone

actor: Embodied-AI runtime and toolchain engineering team (a robotics-software or on-device inference group)
job: Optimizing vision-language-action model inference — quantization, compilation, and scheduling — so heavy manipulation policies execute at control-loop rates on the onboard module.
outcome: A runtime that runs the manipulation policy within control-loop latency on the onboard module, making untethered execution feasible rather than workstation-bound.
motivation: Inference latency, not raw compute alone, is the true tether; closing that gap is what actually unlocks the untethered milestone.
